newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fr Telecom says no negotiations with D Telekom.
newsitem.headline: Fr Telecom says no negotiations with D Telekom.

text.p: State-owned France Telecom denied on Friday a statement by a Deutsche Telekom official that the two telecommunications operators had begun negotiations on swapping a strategic equity stake in order to anchor their European alliance.
"These are regular discussions, we cannot call them negotiations," said a France Telecom spokesman.

He said France Telecom's longstanding position had always been that its alliance with Deutsche Telekom would be "sealed eventually by an equity swap". But this would involve an opening of the capital of France Telecom.
"There is nothing new in all of this," he said.
Joachim Kroeske, Deutsche Telekom's chief finance officer, had said earlier on Friday before leaving for talks with France Telecom in Paris the two companies had begun negotiations over a share swap.
"An equity swap is very likely on the basis of decisions of the companies," he told Reuters Financial Television. "In the long term, there is no doubt."
The Bonn government's decision to sell an additional 25 percent of Deutsche Telekom's capital to strategic investors over the next two years was seen as a first step to such a move.
The second step would be the opening of the capital of France Telecom.

The new French Socialist government, which campaigned on a pledge to halt privatisations, has put the sale of a minority stake in France Telecom planned by the previous conservative administration on hold.
France's Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said this week he was "not against" the idea but wants to consult the telecom operator's staff first.
